label: Product & commerce
intent: Sell one object. The product is the hero and must stay faithful to the real thing.

recipes.goal: A single clean product image for a listing or a paid ad.
recipes.when: You have one product and need the shop-card shot: isolated, well lit, nothing competing.
recipes.text:
Create a {ratio} product photograph of {subject}.
COMPOSITION — {composition}. The product fills roughly two thirds of the frame with clean margin on all sides.
BACKGROUND — {background}, with a soft contact shadow anchoring the product so it does not float.
LIGHTING — {lighting}. One clear light direction; keep the shadow soft-edged and readable.
SURFACE — {surface}.
COLOUR — {grading}. The product's own colours must stay accurate; do not tint them.
RENDER — {render}. Sharp focus across the whole product, no shallow depth of field that blurs the far edge.

image.accepts: a photo of the real product
image.skeleton:
Use the supplied product photograph as the one and only reference for {subject}. Preserve its form, proportions, materials, surface finish and any label or logo text exactly — do not redesign, restyle or re-letter it.

Re-render it as a {ratio} {render}: {composition} on {surface}, with {background} and {lighting}. Grade {grading} but keep the product's own colours accurate. Clean up the background and any lens artefacts from the source. Soft contact shadow under the product. No text, no watermark, no props.

recipes.example: Create a 4:5 product photograph of a matte sage-green glass lotion bottle with a brushed aluminium cap. COMPOSITION — centred hero, filling two thirds of the frame with clean margin. BACKGROUND — seamless warm grey with a soft contact shadow. LIGHTING — softbox key from upper left with a white fill card on the right; the shadow stays soft-edged. SURFACE — seamless paper. COLOUR — neutral and true; the sage green must read exactly as it does in life. RENDER — studio catalogue photography, sharp focus across the whole bottle.

recipes.goal: The product in a believable place, so it reads as part of someone's real day.
recipes.when: The listing shot exists and you need the brand-feel image: the product in use, in a room, on a table, in a hand.
recipes.text:
Create a {ratio} lifestyle photograph of {subject}, placed in a real setting rather than a studio.
SCENE — a believable, lived-in environment that suits the product. Include two or three supporting objects that belong there, none of them competing for attention.
COMPOSITION — {composition}. The product is clearly the subject even though the frame is not empty.
LIGHTING — {lighting}. Let real light fall across the scene and cast natural shadows.
COLOUR — {grading}.
MOOD — {mood}.
RENDER — {render}, with the product in sharp focus and the surroundings softly behind it. Slight imperfection is good: a used surface, a stray crumb, a real shadow.

image.accepts: a photo of the real product
image.skeleton:
Use the supplied product photograph as the exact reference for {subject}. Preserve its form, proportions, materials and label text precisely; do not restyle it.

Place that product into a {ratio} {render} lifestyle scene: {composition}, {lighting}, {grading}, {mood}. Build a believable lived-in setting around it with two or three supporting objects that belong there. The product must remain the sharp, accurate hero of the frame while the surroundings fall softly behind it.

recipes.example: Create a 3:4 lifestyle photograph of a matte ceramic pour-over coffee set, placed on a real kitchen counter rather than a studio backdrop. SCENE — a sunlit kitchen corner: a worn wooden board, a folded linen cloth, a few loose coffee beans. Nothing else competes. COMPOSITION — rule of thirds, the set on the left third, counter space breathing on the right. LIGHTING — natural window light from the right, casting a soft long shadow across the counter. COLOUR — warm muted. MOOD — warm and human, a slow morning. RENDER — editorial photography, the set in sharp focus, the room softly behind it.

recipes.goal: A designed page that shows the product and also explains it.
recipes.when: You need the spec-sheet look: a hero image plus structured detail, for a brand book, a deck or a spec page.
recipes.text:
Create a {ratio} product specification page, laid out as a clean modular grid on a warm neutral paper-like background.
TOP SECTION — lifestyle hero: {subject}, {composition}, on {surface}, lit with {lighting}, generous whitespace around it.
BOTTOM SECTION — technical panel in a tidy modular grid:
- Orthographic line drawings of the product: front, side and three-quarter view, drawn in fine {type} technical weight.
- Three or four short labelled callouts pointing at real features, set in {type} at small size.
COLOUR — {grading}. Keep the drawings monochrome so the hero image carries the colour.
RENDER — the page should read as printed matter, not as a screen.

image.accepts: a photo of the real product
image.skeleton:
Use the supplied product photograph as the exact reference for {subject}. Preserve its form, proportions, materials and label text.

Lay it out as a {ratio} specification page on a warm neutral paper background. TOP — the product as a {composition} hero shot on {surface}, lit with {lighting}, with generous whitespace. BOTTOM — a modular technical panel: orthographic front, side and three-quarter line drawings of the same product in fine {type} weight, plus three or four short labelled callouts at real features. {grading}. The page must read as printed matter.

recipes.example: Create a 3:4 product specification page for a titanium travel mug, laid out on a warm neutral paper background. TOP SECTION — the mug as a centred hero on seamless paper under even flat studio light, with generous whitespace. BOTTOM SECTION — a modular technical panel: orthographic front, side and three-quarter line drawings in fine monospaced technical weight, plus four short labelled callouts for the lid thread, vacuum wall, base ring and handle mount. COLOUR — neutral and true. The whole page should read as printed matter, not as a screen.
